current_example.problem: Write $\dfrac{3x^3}{x^3+4}$ in the form $a + \dfrac{b}{x^3+4},$ where $a \neq 0.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we add and subtract $4$ in parentheses in the numerator. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}+4} & =\frac{3({x}^{3}+4-4)}{{x}^{3}+4} \\  & =\frac{3({x}^{3}+4)+3(-4)}{{x}^{3}+4} \\  & =\frac{3({x}^{3}+4)-12}{{x}^{3}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3({x}^{3}+4)-12}{{x}^{3}+4} & =\frac{3({x}^{3}+4)}{{x}^{3}+4}+\frac{-12}{{x}^{3}+4} \\  & =3+\frac{-12}{{x}^{3}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=3$ and $b=-12,$ and we get

$$
a + b = 3 + (-12) = -9.
$$
